episodes.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
episodes.headline: When context becomes lasting memory
episodes.description: Can useful context survive after the prompt disappears? A careful look at learning new behavior while preserving the old.
episodes.takeaway: Retest older examples after every update, even when the original weights stay frozen.
episodes.caveat: Fifty compatible factual edits are not indefinite lifelong learning. Replay also changes the optimization budget.

episodes.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
episodes.headline: A smaller cache. What survives?
episodes.description: Compress a document’s attention cache for questions that have not been asked yet.
episodes.takeaway: Preserve both what a memory returns and how strongly it competes for attention.
episodes.caveat: 16× describes logical key-value compression, not measured physical memory savings or faster inference. Preparation is expensive.
episodes.thumbnail_changes: Cropped to stage 1; frozen/trainable legend retained. Other stages omitted. This cropped thumbnail is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0; this notice does not license the video or website.

episodes.title: Enhancing Latent World Models with Associative Memory
episodes.headline: Better plans through associative memory
episodes.description: A compact memory bank helps a world model predict latent states and plan from images.
episodes.takeaway: Compact latent conditioning can help planning, but a learned prior is not a growing episodic memory.
episodes.caveat: Small simulation study; no inference-time write rule. The paper does not clearly define its error bars.
episodes.thumbnail_changes: Cropped to memory/predictor detail; surrounding rollout omitted.

episodes.title: TimeCap: A Scalable Open-Source Pipeline for Captioning Wearable Health Time-Series Data
episodes.headline: Auditable captions for wearable signals
episodes.description: Auditable rule-based captions for wearable time series, with preliminary prediction gains and clinical limitations.
episodes.takeaway: Use deterministic signal-language rules when reproducible annotations matter.
episodes.caveat: Self-reported outcomes, only fifteen positive atrial-fibrillation test participants and no external clinical validation; caption access is restricted.

episodes.title: PPG-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for PPG Foundation Models
episodes.headline: Make a foundation model earn its complexity
episodes.description: A controlled benchmark asks when pulse-signal foundation models beat simple physiological and general-purpose controls.
episodes.takeaway: Compare pulse-signal models with constant, physiological-feature and general time-series controls using participant-level evaluation.
episodes.caveat: Retrospective benchmark results do not establish clinical utility. Confidence-interval overlap is not equivalence, and released recipes may not be optimally tuned.

episodes.title: Detecting Agitation Before Behavioral Escalation in Autistic Youth Through Multimodal Wearable Sensing
episodes.headline: Temporal evaluation changes the result
episodes.description: A small personalized sensing study reveals how temporal evaluation changes apparent agitation-detection performance.
episodes.takeaway: Audit personalization, labels, sensor contributions and chronological splits before treating a sensing model as an early-warning system.
episodes.caveat: Fifteen participants in clinician-led sessions; no unseen-child validation or demonstrated prevention of escalation. Earlier windows were not independently labeled as agitation.

episodes.title: Are We Overthinking One-Step Generation?
episodes.headline: Reconstruct first, generate in one step
episodes.description: Reconstruction pretraining improves the quality-compute frontier of one-step image generation.
episodes.takeaway: An easy reconstruction objective can prepare a generator for harder distribution matching; compare the complete quality-compute frontier.
episodes.caveat: Compute multipliers depend on the baseline. Video prediction resets from real observations and does not establish stable simulation or improved control.
episodes.presentation_note: Some labels in the original paper figures are small in this edition. Open the linked paper for full-resolution figures.

episodes.title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization
episodes.headline: Count representation learning in the budget
episodes.description: Representation geometry learned from predictive information is evaluated under a full generative-training compute budget.
episodes.takeaway: Learn representation geometry from conditional prediction advantage and evaluate generation under the full training budget.
episodes.caveat: Large encoder-compute savings are extrapolated scaling projections, not measured end-to-end speedups. No runnable release was verified at review time.
episodes.presentation_note: Some labels in the original paper figures are small in this edition. Open the linked paper for full-resolution figures.

episodes.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
episodes.headline: Continuous thought, explicit tool calls
episodes.description: Continuous internal reasoning combines with explicit text tool calls and persistent mixed attention state.
episodes.takeaway: Combine latent recurrence with text actions and persistent mixed state, then measure complete latency, memory and correctness.
episodes.caveat: The attention cache grows. Estimated decoding cost excludes prompt processing and external tools; readable latent readouts are not proof of faithful explanations.
episodes.presentation_note: Some labels in the original paper figures are small in this edition. Open the linked paper for full-resolution figures.
episodes.thumbnail_changes: Right panel cropped; text/latent-mode labels retained. Adapter detail omitted.

episodes.title: Memorilla: Latent Semantic Memory for LLMs
episodes.headline: A growing vector store, sixteen memory tokens
episodes.description: A learned reader compresses document embeddings into continuous inputs for a frozen language model.
episodes.takeaway: Separate persistent storage from query-conditioned readout.
episodes.caveat: Bounded decoder input does not imply bounded retrieval or storage; substantial supervised training is required.

episodes.title: Teaching PPG How, Not Who: Fixed-Effects Distillation from ECG
episodes.headline: Learn changing physiology, not recording identity
episodes.description: A small bridge learns within-recording changes from electrical heart signals to optical pulse signals.
episodes.takeaway: Subtract stable recording offsets when learning changing physiological state.
episodes.caveat: External blood-pressure prediction fails a simple baseline; patient-disjoint generalization is not established.

episodes.takeaway: Audit individual frequency bands instead of trusting average reconstruction loss.

episodes.title: Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series
episodes.headline: Physical measurements teach a video model what to preserve
episodes.description: A shared video encoder learns from aligned physical-state targets during training, then runs on video alone. Matched controls test whether alignment matters.
episodes.takeaway: Treat synchronized physical measurements as training supervision, and separately test what the frozen representation preserves.
episodes.caveat: These are supervised readout results, not demonstrated wearable deployment, continual learning or universal planning gains.

episodes.title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
episodes.headline: TIDER uses date windows to recover memories semantic search misses
episodes.description: A trained temporal locator adds date-based candidates before answer generation. With the same memory pool and top-20 unit budget, LifeBench accuracy rises from 52.21% to 61.52%; transfer to LoCoMo exposes temporal-localization failures.
episodes.takeaway: Learn when to retrieve, then combine temporal and semantic evidence while keeping the answer model fixed.
episodes.caveat: Synthetic, accurately timestamped histories; LoCoMo temporal accuracy trails TiMem. Gold evidence/date supervision and a costly reinforcement-learning run are required.

episodes.title: BeJEPA: A Goal-Conditioned Humanoid Behavior World Model via Unsupervised RL
episodes.headline: BeJEPA separates immediate physics from goal-conditioned futures
episodes.description: A humanoid policy learns from a next-state predictor and a discounted summary of behavioral continuation. Balanced model-predictive refinement improves global tracking in the paper's simulation protocol, while local posture and hardware evidence remain qualified.
episodes.takeaway: Couple local physical prediction with a goal-conditioned future summary to train world-anchored control.
episodes.caveat: Hardware evidence is qualitative; measured MPC latency and training GPU-hours are unreported. SONIC retains better AMASS local posture, and deployment weights remain frozen.

episodes.title: ECG-SDI: Single-lead Electrocardiogram Enables Continuous Sleep Depth Index Profiling and Scalable Digital Biomarkers for Sleep Health
episodes.headline: ECG-SDI turns sleep stages into a depth score, with a label dependency
episodes.description: A single-lead ECG model learns ordered sleep depth across retrospective cohorts. The review separates raw stage agreement from reference-label-normalized biomarkers and uncontrolled CPAP changes.
episodes.takeaway: An accessible ECG research direction, with strong cohort evidence but no label-free home validation.
episodes.caveat: Normalized outputs and several biomarkers use reference sleep stages; uncertainty bootstraps epochs and wearable accuracy is unmeasured.

episodes.title: PulseBound: Future-Beat State Forecasting Under an Explicit Information Boundary
episodes.headline: PulseBound closes a hidden future-data channel before preprocessing
episodes.description: Prefix-only normalization and suffix replacement make future-beat prediction auditable. Matched forecasting and transfer gains come with explicit tokenizer, preprocessing and dataset-split limits.
episodes.takeaway: The reusable idea is an information-access contract that can be attacked and tested.
episodes.caveat: The frozen tokenizer saw full processed MIMIC before its patient split; the audit starts after upstream preprocessing and device feasibility is unmeasured.

episodes.title: Few-Shot Prototype Head Adaptation for On-Device ECG Personalization on PSoC 6
episodes.headline: Tiny ECG personalization works on an MCU, but its patient split needs repair
episodes.description: Frozen embeddings and class means provide lightweight ECG personalization on PSoC 6. An independent code-and-dataset audit finds one participant crossing the development/test boundary.
episodes.takeaway: The hardware measurements are useful; population-generalization claims need a corrected split and external validation.
episodes.caveat: Records 201 and 202 belong to the same person but are assigned to DS1 and DS2; no corrected rerun quantifies the impact. The 17× timing claim is host-only.

episodes.title: HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents
episodes.headline: HexaShell turns robot failures into reusable code repairs
episodes.description: A fixed coding model uses calibrated cameras, geometric measurements and a repair agent to develop robot tools. Frozen tools reach 39.7% success under RoboDojo's aggregation, while fine contact and paused-simulation latency remain substantial limitations.
episodes.takeaway: Persistent software repairs can improve simulated manipulation without changing model weights.
episodes.caveat: The leaderboard comparison uses different evaluation samples; development includes inherited tools and human assistance, and the full harness is not released.

episodes.title: BizAgentBench: Unveiling Hidden Challenges in Deploying Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Business
episodes.headline: BizAgentBench checks whether every business action stayed valid
episodes.description: A synthetic payments benchmark scores goal attainment, valid process and protection of records across complete execution histories. Deterministic checks reveal gaps hidden by final-state success and test the effect of supplying documents and customer facts.
episodes.takeaway: An acceptable final result is insufficient when a workflow can violate constraints along the way.
episodes.caveat: Fifty synthetic tasks do not certify real-world safety. Unequal repetitions and a small sample limit model-ranking claims.

episodes.title: Speculative Sampling in Interactive Video Generation
episodes.headline: Interactive video generation: predict a large future, commit it in small pieces
episodes.description: A serving controller caches joint video predictions, releases a small protected prefix and replaces uncommitted futures when instructions change. Matched large-chunk experiments improve responsiveness, but a short-chunk LTX setting becomes slower and stalls more.
episodes.takeaway: Separate prediction size from commitment size, then measure response time, stalls and total resource use together.
episodes.caveat: Benefits depend on model, scheduling and hardware. Frequent updates waste predictions, and lower per-GPU activity is not evidence of lower total cost.

episodes.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
episodes.headline: Must-read: trained read/write memory changes per-conversation state without retraining the backbone
episodes.description: Must-read: trained read/write memory changes per-conversation state without retraining the backbone; compare compression against recall fidelity.
episodes.takeaway: Token-level updates and response training matter more than branding.
episodes.caveat: The most useful ablation replaces token-level writes with one turn-level update: Nano’s average falls from forty-seven to forty-one. Removing response post-training falls further, to thirty-six point three. Changing the exact gated update formula has a much smaller effect. The reusable idea is therefore a learned write-and-read interface, not just a named update rule. For continual agents, test latent state alongside exact retrieval at matched evidence budgets. Measure forgotten details, not only bytes. Fixed state remains lossy, and autonomous experience acquisition and consolidation remain open problems.

episodes.title: ACCRUE: Continual Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Robot Foundation Models
episodes.headline: Continual robot RL separates new-task reward learning from old-task action matching, with important growing-memory and cost caveats.
episodes.description: Continual robot RL separates new-task reward learning from old-task action matching, with important growing-memory and cost caveats.
episodes.takeaway: Separate the roles of value transfer and behavioral memory.
episodes.caveat: The hardware stopping rule is nineteen successes in a rolling window of twenty episodes. There is no full hardware baseline sweep, and related assemblies may transfer more readily than unrelated tasks. Resetting the critic modestly worsens performance; updating it on old replay also hurts retention. However, the visual-encoder ablation changes both encoder identity and stability, so it cannot isolate representation drift. The key reusable design is to separate current reward learning from prior behavior preservation. Code is marked coming soon. Official footage is linked, not reproduced here.
